newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON JOGS THROUGH OPENING ROUND.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON JOGS THROUGH OPENING ROUND.

text.p: Michael Johnson jogged through his opening 400 metres race on the second day of the world championships on Sunday with minimum effort and no apparent after-effects from the injury which has disrupted his season.
The Olympic 200-400 metres champion clocked 45.66 seconds in front of a small crowd scattered throughout the Olympic stadium.
"I came in confident," Johnson said. "My objective is just to get through every round as comfortably and easily as possible.
"Up until this point the season has been very frustrating but I am glad to be healthy now."

Johnson injured his left quadriceps in the 150 metres showdown with Donovan Bailey on June 1 and suffered his first defeat over 400 for eight years later the same month when he lost to 1991 champion Antonio Pettigrew in Paris.
He returned to Texas for further training and to await a decision by the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) on the vexed issue of awarding wild cards to defending champions.
To nobody's surprise, the IAAF decided it could not stage a championships without its biggest attraction and Johnson travelled to Athens to defend his 400 title.
Jamaican long jumper James Beckford was the first beneficiary of the IAAF's decision to scrap three months suspensions for first offenders testing positive for stimulants.
Beckford was suspended after testing positive for ephedrine in Paris on June 25 and would not have been allowed to compete here under the old regulations.
He took advantage on Sunday by finishing third in his qualifying round behind defending champion Ivan Pedroso of Cuba.
Maurice Wignall, another Jamaican who is a student at George Mason University in Fairfax, Virginia, headed the first qualifying group with a personal best of 8.09.
Olympic silver medallist Joe Greene of the United States failed to qualify for Tuesday's final.
Germany's former world champion Sabine Braun led the heptathlon with 2,206 points after the first two events followed by Britain's Olympic bronze medallist Denise Lewis.
